profile.goal: No goal race - open-ended base building. Run farther and faster while feeling strong, lower average HR (aerobic efficiency + resting HR trend), build muscle, ride bike opportunistically.
profile.rest_day_policy: No fixed rest day - readiness (sleep/HRV/RHR/Body Battery/Garmin composite scores) decides day to day
profile.gym_split: 3x/week: Chest/Tri early week, Back/Bi later week, Legs on Sunday
profile.bike_policy: Flexible/ad hoc, roughly 1x/week, used when running isn't the right call that day - not a fixed training pillar
profile.quality_day_note: Athlete goal ('heart beating more efficiently, more blood/O2 per beat, lower HR over time') is served by two distinct stimuli: aerobic base volume (genuinely easy Z1/Z2) drives capillarization/mitochondrial/resting-HR adaptations, while deliberate hard/interval work drives stroke-volume and cardiac-output adaptations. Both matter - a planned interval session is not a violation of the easy-day rule, it's the other half of the goal. Confirmed with athlete 2026-07-22. Future plan files should mark quality/interval sessions explicitly when scheduled so weekly hard-day stacking logic accounts for them.
profile.known_issue: Three straight easy-day HR overshoots (07-14, 07-17, 07-19) all happened on trail/hilly routes. Garmin's own Training Status flagged 'Unproductive - Low Aerobic Shortage' over the trailing 4 weeks, corroborating this independently. This week's easy days are deliberately routed flat/road to isolate terrain as a variable.
profile.heat_context: Little Rock under an Extreme Heat Warning through Tue 07-21 evening: highs ~100F, heat index 105-115F, overnight lows stuck in the 80s (source: NWS / arkansasonline.com, checked 2026-07-20). A cooler front arrives Wed but highs stay mid-upper 90s through at least Thu. Poor overnight cooling likely contributes to Garmin's 'High Recovery Need' reading independent of training discipline, and heat legitimately raises HR at a given pace. Athlete confirmed on 2026-07-20 he's good training through this heat and wants to keep the original volume plan - schedule unchanged, but hydrate well and treat any dizziness/nausea/stopped sweating as a hard stop.

flags: Garmin's own Training Status (Unproductive - Low Aerobic Shortage, trailing 4 weeks) independently corroborates the recurring 'easy days running hot' pattern flagged since 07-14. The fix isn't more effort, it's genuinely easier easy days - heat is a real additional confound this week (see heat_context) but athlete has chosen to train through it rather than adjust the schedule.

Tuesday and Wednesday's easy runs are deliberately routed flat/road (not the usual trail routes) to test whether terrain, not effort, has been driving the HR overshoots. Heat may also elevate HR independent of terrain this week - worth noting if Tuesday still overshoots despite the flat route.
